 1   I.   Introduction
 2        Q.   PLEASE      STATE       YOUR         NAME,    BUSINESS        ADDRESS,       AND

 3             OCCUPATION.

 4        A.   My name is Jaime Lyndsey McGovern. My business address is Always Building,

 5             814 Respect Dr, Bentonville, AR 72716, MS:5530. I am employed by Walmart Inc.

 6             (“Walmart”) as Senior Manager, Utility Partnerships - Regulatory.

 7        Q.   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU TESTIFYING IN THIS DOCKET?

 8        A.   I am testifying on behalf of Walmart.

 9        Q.   PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE.

10        A.   I hold a PhD and a Master of Science in economics from the W.P. Carey School of

11             Business at Arizona State University. I also earned a Bachelor of Arts in economics

12             and mathematics from Arizona State University. I served as a utility analyst at the

13             Oregon Public Utility Commission from 2006-2008 and held the role of Assistant

14             Professor of Economics at SUNY Fredonia and SUNY Oneonta, 2005-2006 and

15             2008-2010, respectively. I was the Senior Energy Economist at the Citizen’s Utility

16             Board of Oregon from 2013-2018, and the Policy Analyst and Energy Economist

17             at The Utility Reform Network of California (“TURN”) from 2023-2024. At the

18             Oregon Legislature, I was the Revenue Economist responsible for energy, natural

19             resources, forestry, property, and telecommunications from 2017-2023. My

20             Witness Qualifications Statement is attached as Exhibit JLM-1.

21        Q.   ARE YOU THE SAME DR. JAIME MCGOVERN WHO SUBMITTED

22             DIRECT TESTIMONY ON BEHALF OF WALMART IN THIS CASE?


                                                1
                                            NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT

                                  in Support of Stipulation on behalf of Walmart Inc.


 1              A.       Yes, I am.

 2              Q.       HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY BEFORE OTHER

 3                       STATE REGULATORY COMMISSIONS?

 4              A.       Yes, I have submitted testimony with Oregon Public Utility Commission, the

 5                       California Public Utility Commission, the Washington Utilities and Transportation

 6                       Commission, and the Utah Public Service Commission in the cases listed under

 7                       “Commission Dockets” in Exhibit JLM-1.

 8              Q.       ARE YOU SPONSORING EXHIBITS IN YOUR TESTIMONY?

 9              A.       Yes. I am sponsoring the Exhibit listed in the Table of Contents.

10              Q.       PLEASE BRIEFLY DESCRIBE WALMART’S OPERATIONS IN NEW

11                       MEXICO.

12              A.       As shown on Walmart’s website, Walmart operates 52 retail units, 1 distribution

13                       center, and employs over 15,000 associates in New Mexico. In fiscal year ending

14                       2024, Walmart purchased $138.7 million worth of goods and services from New

15                       Mexico-based suppliers, supporting over 6,000 supplier jobs. 1

16              Q.       PLEASE BRIEFLY DESCRIBE WALMART’S OPERATIONS WITHIN

17                       SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S (“SPS” or

18                       “Company”) SERVICE TERRITORY.


19              A.      Walmart has six retail stores that take electric service from SPS in New Mexico,

20                      primarily on the Company’s Secondary General Service (“SG”) schedule.

 1   II.         Purpose of Testimony and Summary of Recommendations
 2               Q.       WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

 3               A.       The purpose of my testimony is to support the Comprehensive Stipulation

 4                        (“Stipulation”) filed with the Commission on June 22, 2026, among the following

 5                        parties (collectively, “Signatories”): (i) the Company, New Mexico Large

 6                        Customer Group (“NMLCG”), Occidental Permian Ltd. (“OPL”), Louisiana

 7                        Energy Services LLC (“LES”), Federal Executive Agencies (“FEA”), Targa

 8                        Resources Corp. (“Targa”), Walmart Inc. (“Walmart”), Coalition for Clean

 9                        Affordable Energy (“CCAE”), and Prosperity Works. Commission Utility Division

10                        Staff (“Staff”) does not oppose parts of the Stipulation, which it will articulate in

11                        its Statement of Opposition. The New Mexico Energy, Minerals, and Natural

12                        Resources Department (“EMNRD”) takes no position on the Stipulation. 2

13               Q.       WAS WALMART AN ACTIVE PARTICIPANT IN SETTLEMENT

14                        DISCUSSIONS IN THIS PROCEEDING?

15               A.       Yes.

16               Q.       WHAT IS WALMART’S RECOMMENDATION TO THE COMMISSION?

17               A.       Walmart recommends the Commission approve the Stipulation as a reasonable

18                        resolution of the specific issues addressed in the Stipulation. The Stipulation is the

19                        result of arms-length negotiations among the Signatories and addresses Walmart’s

20                        issues presented during settlement discussions. Walmart believes that the result of

21                        the negotiations contained in the Stipulation would be just and reasonable rates that



     2
         Stipulation, p. 1.

                                                            3
                           NMPRC Case No. 25-00079-UT

1        are in the public interest, and approval of the Stipulation would yield a just,

2        equitable, and reasonable resolution of all issues that were or could have been raised

3        by the parties in this proceeding.

4   Q.   DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR TESTIMONY?

5   A.   Yes.
